claims.claim: **Most toddler ingestions are insignificant**, but ⚠️ **at this age, just 1–2 tablets of certain agents can be highly toxic.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Poisoning - Acute Guidelines For Initial Management' (Last updated August 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Poisoning_-_Acute_Guidelines_For_Initial_Management/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Resuscitation and risk assessment may need to run concurrently; most treatment is supportive.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Poisoning - Acute Guidelines For Initial Management' (Last updated August 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Poisoning_-_Acute_Guidelines_For_Initial_Management/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **All intentional self-poisonings in adolescents need a paracetamol screen and admission.** Take every act of deliberate self-harm extremely seriously.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Poisoning - Acute Guidelines For Initial Management' (Last updated August 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Poisoning_-_Acute_Guidelines_For_Initial_Management/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Consider non-accidental injury or neglect** when the poisoning doesn't fit the child's developmental age, the history is inconsistent, or there is past poisoning, illicit drugs or unusual household-substance poisoning. **An infant under 1 cannot take medicines by themselves.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Poisoning - Acute Guidelines For Initial Management' (Last updated August 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Poisoning_-_Acute_Guidelines_For_Initial_Management/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Check any unconscious patient for a Medicalert bracelet** or other signs of an underlying condition.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Poisoning - Acute Guidelines For Initial Management' (Last updated August 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Poisoning_-_Acute_Guidelines_For_Initial_Management/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Potentially lethal in 1–3 tablets:** tricyclic antidepressants · theophylline · beta blockers · sulphonylureas (**onset of hypoglycaemia may be delayed by 8 hours**) · calcium channel blockers (delayed bradycardia, hypotension) · ecstasy and other amphetamines · chloroquine/hydroxychloroquine.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Poisoning - Acute Guidelines For Initial Management' (Last updated August 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Poisoning_-_Acute_Guidelines_For_Initial_Management/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Potentially harmful in 1–3 tablets or small exposures (selected):** baclofen 25 mg (coma) · camphor · carbamazepine 400 mg (coma) · clonidine · clozapine · corrosives · hydrocarbons and essential oils · paraquat · venlafaxine 150 mg (seizures).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Poisoning - Acute Guidelines For Initial Management' (Last updated August 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Poisoning_-_Acute_Guidelines_For_Initial_Management/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Ring Poisons Information (13 11 26)** with: agent and formulation (immediate or modified release) · route · time · **dose per kg, counting everything that could have been in the pack** · weight · symptoms and signs. **Beware mixed overdose and inaccurate dose reporting.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Poisoning - Acute Guidelines For Initial Management' (Last updated August 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Poisoning_-_Acute_Guidelines_For_Initial_Management/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Mixed or unknown ingestion: check a paracetamol level.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Poisoning - Acute Guidelines For Initial Management' (Last updated August 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Poisoning_-_Acute_Guidelines_For_Initial_Management/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **A poisoned child may be unable to protect the airway even at >GCS8**; AVPU may describe conscious state better.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Poisoning - Acute Guidelines For Initial Management' (Last updated August 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Poisoning_-_Acute_Guidelines_For_Initial_Management/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Dysrhythmias:** sodium-channel blockade → **sodium bicarbonate**; potassium-channel blockade → **magnesium sulphate**.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Poisoning - Acute Guidelines For Initial Management' (Last updated August 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Poisoning_-_Acute_Guidelines_For_Initial_Management/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Poisoning seizures: benzodiazepines first, barbiturates second.** ⚠️ **Phenytoin is not recommended** (usually ineffective).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Poisoning - Acute Guidelines For Initial Management' (Last updated August 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Poisoning_-_Acute_Guidelines_For_Initial_Management/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Check glucose; treat if under 4 mmol/L.** Think of drug-induced syndromes: neuroleptic malignant syndrome, serotonin syndrome, malignant hyperthermia.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Poisoning - Acute Guidelines For Initial Management' (Last updated August 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Poisoning_-_Acute_Guidelines_For_Initial_Management/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Temperature above 38.5 °C needs urgent cooling.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Poisoning - Acute Guidelines For Initial Management' (Last updated August 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Poisoning_-_Acute_Guidelines_For_Initial_Management/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Eye:** copious saline irrigation (local anaesthetic drops and sedation may be needed). **Skin:** take the clothes off, rinse with plenty of water, then wash with soap and water.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Poisoning - Acute Guidelines For Initial Management' (Last updated August 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Poisoning_-_Acute_Guidelines_For_Initial_Management/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Discuss every gut-decontamination method with a toxicologist first** — **activated charcoal has killed children.** **In hospital, emesis has no place.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Poisoning - Acute Guidelines For Initial Management' (Last updated August 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Poisoning_-_Acute_Guidelines_For_Initial_Management/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Activated charcoal has a very limited role:** not without a toxicologist, **unless the child arrives within 1 hour of a potentially toxic ingestion and is fully conscious.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Poisoning - Acute Guidelines For Initial Management' (Last updated August 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Poisoning_-_Acute_Guidelines_For_Initial_Management/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Charcoal contraindications:** altered conscious state · cyanide · fluoride · hydrocarbons · alkalis/corrosives · mineral acids (boric acid) · ethanol/glycols · metals including lithium, iron and potassium.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Poisoning - Acute Guidelines For Initial Management' (Last updated August 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Poisoning_-_Acute_Guidelines_For_Initial_Management/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Gastric lavage:** very limited role, needs intubation, only after consultation. **Whole bowel irrigation:** a limited role when a life-threatening ingestion involves certain slow-release preparations or agents charcoal doesn't bind.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Poisoning - Acute Guidelines For Initial Management' (Last updated August 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Poisoning_-_Acute_Guidelines_For_Initial_Management/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Antidote pairings (selected):** flumazenil for benzodiazepines · glucagon for beta blocker · digoxin immune Fab for digoxin · desferrioxamine for iron · pyridoxine for isoniazid · Intralipid for local anaesthetics · methylene blue for methaemoglobinaemia · naloxone for opiates · octreotide for oral hypoglycaemics · N-acetylcysteine for paracetamol · sodium bicarbonate for tricyclic antidepressants · vitamin K for warfarin/long-acting rodenticide.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Poisoning - Acute Guidelines For Initial Management' (Last updated August 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Poisoning_-_Acute_Guidelines_For_Initial_Management/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Calcium channel blocker:** Intralipid, insulin/glucose, calcium. **Cyanide:** sodium thiosulphate, dicobalt edetate, hydroxocobalamin.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Poisoning - Acute Guidelines For Initial Management' (Last updated August 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Poisoning_-_Acute_Guidelines_For_Initial_Management/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Urinary alkalinisation helps salicylate toxicity if done meticulously.** **Multi-dose charcoal** has a pharmacokinetic effect but no evident improvement in clinical outcome.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Poisoning - Acute Guidelines For Initial Management' (Last updated August 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Poisoning_-_Acute_Guidelines_For_Initial_Management/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Small water-soluble toxins are cleared by intermittent high-flux haemodialysis**: lithium, salicylate, valproate, theophylline, methotrexate, barbiturates, toxic alcohols. CVVH is only for patients who can't tolerate haemodialysis.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Poisoning - Acute Guidelines For Initial Management' (Last updated August 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Poisoning_-_Acute_Guidelines_For_Initial_Management/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider admission for every adolescent with an intentional overdose.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Poisoning - Acute Guidelines For Initial Management' (Last updated August 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Poisoning_-_Acute_Guidelines_For_Initial_Management/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Transfer** when care is needed beyond the local hospital and paediatric team. **PIPER (Victoria): 1300 137 650.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Poisoning - Acute Guidelines For Initial Management' (Last updated August 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Poisoning_-_Acute_Guidelines_For_Initial_Management/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Intentional self-harm → local mental health services** (e.g. Orygen 1800 888 320). **Recreational poisoning → YoDAA** (1800 458 685).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Poisoning - Acute Guidelines For Initial Management' (Last updated August 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Poisoning_-_Acute_Guidelines_For_Initial_Management/, retrieved 2026-09-23
